The first thing we notice is that we can rewrite the terms of the series as powers of $\frac{e}{3}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}1-\frac{e}{3}+\frac{{e}^{2}}{9}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}{e}^{n}}{{3}^{n}}+⋯ & =1-\frac{e}{3}+\frac{{e}^{2}}{{3}^{2}}+⋯+(-1)^{n}\frac{{e}^{n}}{{3}^{n}}+⋯ \\  & =1-\frac{e}{3}+{(\frac{e}{3})}^{2}+⋯+(-1)^{n}{(\frac{e}{3})}^{n}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we recognize that the series looks similar to the Maclaurin expansion for $f(x)=\frac{1}{1+x}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{1+x} & =1-x+{x}^{2}-{x}^{3}+⋯+(-1)^{n}{x}^{n}+⋯\,\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{e}{3}$ into our Maclaurin expansion gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{(1+\frac{e}{3})} & =1-\frac{e}{3}+{(\frac{e}{3})}^{2}-{(\frac{e}{3})}^{3}+⋯+(-1)^{n}{(\frac{e}{3})}^{n}+⋯ \\ \frac{3}{3+e} & =1-\frac{e}{3}+\frac{{e}^{2}}{9}-\frac{{e}^{3}}{27}+⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}{e}^{n}}{{3}^{n}}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the sum of the series is $\frac{3}{3+e}.$
